note: A stylized map of the biblical world. The main panel is the land of Israel; the strip above holds the wider world of empire and epistle — Babylon to Rome.

places.name: Egypt (Goshen)
places.desc: Granary of the ancient world — where Joseph rose from prison to palace, Israel grew into a nation, and Moses met Pharaoh. 'Out of Egypt have I called my son.'

places.name: Red Sea
places.desc: The waters that stood as a wall while Israel crossed dry-shod — the Old Testament's defining act of deliverance, sung from Exodus 15 to the Psalms.

places.name: Mount Sinai (Horeb)
places.desc: The mountain of the burning bush, the Ten Commandments, and the still small voice that reached Elijah forty days' journey from Jezreel.

places.name: Wilderness of the Wandering
places.desc: Forty years of manna, murmuring, and the long discipline that turned freed slaves into a covenant people.

places.name: Beersheba
places.desc: The well of the oath at the southern edge of the land — 'from Dan even to Beersheba.' Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob all dug in here.

places.name: Gaza (Philistia)
places.desc: Chief of the five Philistine cities — Samson's stage and prison, and the seedbed of Israel's longest border war.

places.name: Hebron
places.desc: Burial place of the patriarchs at Machpelah and David's first capital, seven years before Jerusalem.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.desc: Ruth's harvest fields, David's boyhood pastures, Micah's prophecy — and the manger where the Son of God was born.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.desc: The city of Melchizedek, David, and the temple; of Isaiah's visions and Jeremiah's tears; of Gethsemane, Golgotha, and the empty tomb; of Pentecost. The axis of all four volumes of scripture.

places.name: Jericho
places.desc: The city whose walls fell flat at the seventh trumpet — later home of blind Bartimaeus and little Zacchaeus's sycamore.

places.name: River Jordan
places.desc: Israel's border and baptistery: crossed on dry ground by Joshua, doubled by Elijah's mantle, and hallowed forever when John baptized Jesus in its waters.

places.name: The Salt Sea
places.desc: The lowest place on earth, shadowed by Sodom's memory — Ezekiel saw its waters healed by a river from the temple.

places.name: Bethel
places.desc: 'The house of God' — where Jacob dreamed of the ladder and vowed his vow, and where Israel later set up a rival altar.

places.name: Shiloh
places.desc: Resting place of the tabernacle for three centuries — where Hannah prayed silently and the child Samuel heard his name in the night.

places.name: Samaria
places.desc: Capital of the northern kingdom, Ahab's ivory city — and in the New Testament the well country where Jesus taught a woman about living water.

places.name: Mount Carmel
places.desc: Elijah's mountain of decision: 'How long halt ye between two opinions?' Fire fell, and the prophets of Baal did not answer.

places.name: Nazareth
places.desc: The hill town where the Word of God grew up as a carpenter's son — 'Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?'

places.name: Sea of Galilee
places.desc: The lake at the heart of the ministry: fishermen called, storms stilled, and five thousand fed on its shores.

places.name: Capernaum
places.desc: Jesus's adopted hometown and ministry headquarters — Peter's house, the centurion's faith, the paralytic through the roof.

places.name: Damascus
places.desc: The ancient oasis city on whose road Saul of Tarsus saw a light above the brightness of the sun.

places.name: Babylon
places.desc: The empire that burned Jerusalem and carried Judah captive — Daniel's court, Ezekiel's river, and the psalm that begins 'By the rivers of Babylon.'

places.name: Nineveh
places.desc: 'That great city' of the Assyrians — spared a generation when it repented at Jonah's preaching, and fallen by Nahum's day.

places.name: Susa (Shushan)
places.desc: Winter palace of Persia, where Esther was made queen 'for such a time as this' and Nehemiah served the king his cup.

places.name: Antioch
places.desc: Third city of the empire, first place the disciples were called Christians, and home base of Paul's missionary journeys.

places.name: Ephesus
places.desc: City of Diana's temple where Paul labored three years — later addressed in Ephesians and first of Revelation's seven churches.

places.name: Athens
places.desc: Where Paul stood on Mars' Hill among the philosophers and preached the Unknown God 'in whom we live, and move, and have our being.'

places.name: Corinth
places.desc: The bustling, brawling port church Paul loved, corrected, and wrote his greatest chapter on charity to.

places.name: Patmos
places.desc: The prison island 'for the word of God' where John, in the Spirit on the Lord's day, saw the Revelation.

places.name: Rome
places.desc: Head of the empire and end of the book of Acts — Paul preached two years in his own hired house, 'no man forbidding him.'
